accepted.s: The Dutch factory at Pulicat was established in which year?
accepted.x: The Dutch established their factory at Pulicat in 1610 after taking the site from the Portuguese.
accepted.tq: Use the year-place association to distinguish closely spaced Dutch establishments.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s: Who permitted the Dutch to establish their factory at Machilipatnam?
accepted.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda permitted Van der Haghen to establish the Dutch factory at Machilipatnam.
accepted.tq: Identify the local ruler associated with the trading privilege.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Dutch factory at Pulicat is correct?
o: It was established with the permission of the ruler of Travancore.
It was taken from the English and became the Dutch headquarters in Bengal.
It was taken from the Portuguese and served as the Coromandel headquarters until 1690.
It was established in 1658 and remained the Dutch headquarters until 1824.
accepted.x: Pulicat was taken from the Portuguese, and Fort Geldria at Pulicat served as the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel until 1690.
accepted.tq: Combine the location, predecessor and duration to reject partially altered statements.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bheemunipatnam — 1641
2. Palakollu — 1652
3. Jagannathapuram — 1736
4. Koringa — 1802
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bheemunipatnam, Palakollu, Jagannathapuram and Koringa are associated respectively with 1641, 1652, 1736 and 1802.
accepted.tq: Check each year-place pair before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s: Which of the following was a subordinate Dutch factory in the Krishna–Godavari weaving belt?
accepted.x: Draksharama was one of the subordinate Dutch factories in the Krishna–Godavari weaving belt; the other places are associated with Dutch activity outside that factory network.
accepted.tq: Distinguish subordinate Andhra factories from major overseas centres and battle sites.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s: Which European power had traded at Machilipatnam before the establishment of the first Dutch factory there?
accepted.x: The Portuguese had traded at Machilipatnam before the Dutch established their factory there.
accepted.tq: Use the earlier-presence distinction rather than the later factory chronology.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s: The Dutch were the first European traders in Andhra to obtain the right to do which of the following?
o: Issue farmans in their own name
accepted.x: The Dutch were the first to obtain the right to mint coins in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive privilege with the correct European power.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories in Andhra → year and order; earlier Portuguese presence

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Pulicat was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia, not a centre of porcelain production. Koringa was associated with shipbuilding and Chittavalasa with jute.
accepted.tq: Find the option that substitutes a trade activity not associated with the stated port.
accepted.sec: Coromandel textile ports and trade items

accepted.s: Which of the following commodities was imported into the Coromandel ports by the Dutch?
accepted.x: Silk and porcelain were imported, whereas gems, diamonds, indigo, cotton, Kalamkari and cloth were among the exports.
accepted.tq: Separate imports from the longer list of export commodities.
accepted.sec: Coromandel textile ports and trade items

accepted.s: In the Dutch carrying trade, Coromandel textiles were exchanged particularly for which commodity from the East Indies?
accepted.x: The Dutch carried textiles from the Coromandel in exchange for spices from the East Indies.
accepted.tq: Trace the direction and purpose of the carrying trade instead of memorising isolated commodities.
accepted.sec: Coromandel textile ports and trade items

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations contains only commodities or goods associated with Dutch trade through the Coromandel network?
o: Saltpetre from Bihar, opium, rice and pepper from Malabar
Tea from Assam, coal from Bengal and silk from China
Coffee from Ceylon, tobacco from America and wheat from Europe
Gold from Africa, wool from England and sugar from the Caribbean
accepted.x: The Dutch trade network carried saltpetre from Bihar, opium and rice, and pepper from Malabar in addition to Coromandel textiles.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete regional commodity combination and eliminate unrelated trade systems.
accepted.sec: Coromandel textile ports and trade items

accepted.s: Pulicat was also associated with which activity in relation to Batavia?
accepted.x: Pulicat served as a hub of the Dutch slave trade to Batavia.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an auxiliary commercial activity from the principal textile trade.
accepted.sec: Coromandel textile ports and trade items

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Dutch factories in chronological order of establishment:
A. Surat
B. Chinsura
C. Karaikal
D. Nagapattinam
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Surat (1616), Karaikal (1645), Chinsura (1653) and Nagapattinam (1658).
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest years first, then resolve the middle pair.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories elsewhere → year; earliest and chief factory

accepted.s: Which Dutch factory was established in 1645?
accepted.x: The Dutch factory at Karaikal was established in 1645.
accepted.tq: Link the exact year with the corresponding factory.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories elsewhere → year; earliest and chief factory

accepted.s: Nagapattinam became the chief Dutch factory after the decline of which centre in 1690?
accepted.x: Pulicat was the chief Dutch centre until 1690, after which Nagapattinam became the chief factory.
accepted.tq: Test the succession between the former and later chief centres.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories elsewhere → year; earliest and chief factory

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a Dutch centre mentioned in connection with their Indian establishments?
accepted.x: Mahe was a French centre, although it is sometimes incorrectly included in lists of Dutch centres. Kasimbazar, Balasore and Vengurla were associated with Dutch establishments.
accepted.tq: Use the confusable European-centre distinction to identify the exception.
accepted.sec: Dutch factories elsewhere → year; earliest and chief factory

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Dutch establishment at Cochin is correct?
o: It was founded by the Dutch in 1605 and abandoned in 1690.
It was taken from Travancore in 1741 and returned to Portugal in 1824.
It was taken from the Portuguese in 1663 and passed to the British in 1795.
It was taken from the English in 1663 and ceded to the French in 1795.
accepted.x: The Dutch took Cochin from the Portuguese in 1663; it later passed to the British in 1795.
accepted.tq: Keep the predecessor, takeover year and later successor together as one sequence.
accepted.sec: Terms of Dutch settlement; later fate of Cochin

accepted.s: The remaining Dutch settlements, including Pulicat, were ceded under which treaty?
accepted.x: The remaining Dutch settlements, including Pulicat, were ceded under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824.
accepted.tq: Associate the treaty with the final transfer of Dutch settlements.
accepted.sec: Terms of Dutch settlement; later fate of Cochin

accepted.s: The Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC) was formed on:
accepted.x: The VOC was formed on 20 March 1602 by merging Dutch companies. The year 1592 is a commonly noted misprint.
accepted.tq: Reject the near-date trap by retaining the exact formation date.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: The VOC was created by merging:
accepted.x: The VOC was formed through the merger of Dutch companies in 1602.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional origin rather than the company’s later activities.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: Which of the following powers was NOT granted to the VOC by the Dutch States-General?
accepted.x: The VOC received sovereign powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties; it had no power to crown the British monarch.
accepted.tq: Find the authority that lies outside the charter’s sovereign commercial powers.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: What was the headquarters of the VOC in Asia?
accepted.x: Batavia, now Jakarta, was the Asian headquarters of the VOC.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Asian headquarters of the VOC from its Indian headquarters.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: The principal focus of the VOC in Asia was the:
accepted.x: The VOC primarily focused on the Spice Islands, while India was not its central strategic focus.
accepted.tq: Identify the company’s strategic priority rather than its secondary Indian activities.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the background of Dutch expansion in Asia?
o: Philip II — ban on Lisbon trade
Philip II — formation of the VOC in 1602
accepted.x: Philip II’s ban on Lisbon trade formed part of the background to Dutch expansion. Linschoten wrote the Itinerario, while Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596.
accepted.tq: Match each person or event with the correct role in the background sequence.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: The work *Itinerario*, published in 1595–96, is associated with:
accepted.x: Jan Huyghen van Linschoten’s *Itinerario* of 1595–96 provided important information that assisted Dutch expansion.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the writer of the travel account from the later navigator and commanders.
accepted.sec: VOC - formation, charter, headquarters in Asia

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Battle of Colachel of 1741?
o: The English defeated the Dutch and captured Chinsura.
The Dutch defeated Travancore and secured Malabar.
The Portuguese defeated Travancore and recovered Cochin.
Travancore defeated the Dutch and ended their ambitions in Malabar.
accepted.x: Travancore under Marthanda Varma defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741, ending Dutch ambitions in Malabar.
accepted.tq: Match the battle with its opponents and strategic consequence.
accepted.sec: Battles of Colachel and Bedara/Chinsura

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Bedara or Chinsura:
1. It was fought in 1759.
2. The English defeated the Dutch.
3. Francis Forde commanded the English forces.
4. The Dutch subsequently withdrew to Indonesia.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The English defeated the Dutch at Bedara/Chinsura in 1759, with Francis Forde as commander, after which the Dutch withdrew to Indonesia.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, opponents, commander and consequence as a connected battle profile.
accepted.sec: Battles of Colachel and Bedara/Chinsura

accepted.s: Who commanded the Dutch forces at the Battle of Bedara or Chinsura?
accepted.x: J.B. Russell commanded the Dutch forces at the Battle of Bedara/Chinsura in 1759.
accepted.tq: Separate the commanders of the opposing forces in the same battle.
accepted.sec: Battles of Colachel and Bedara/Chinsura

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of Dutch power in India?
o: Their Coromandel cloth trade was always more profitable than Indonesian spices.
They were supported by the English against all Indian powers.
They completely abandoned maritime trade after 1605.
Their priority was the Indonesian spice monopoly rather than Indian territorial expansion.
accepted.x: The Dutch prioritised their spice monopoly in Indonesia, while Malabar was less profitable to them than the Coromandel cloth trade. This weakened their long-term commitment to India.
accepted.tq: Choose the strategic explanation that links commercial priority with imperial decline.
accepted.sec: Decline of the Dutch in India - causes

accepted.s: The Anglo-Dutch conferences of 1613 and 1615 were significant because they:
o: failed to resolve the rivalry between the English and the Dutch
ended the Dutch spice monopoly in Indonesia
established Dutch control over all Indian ports
accepted.x: The conferences of 1613 and 1615 failed to settle the fierce Anglo-Dutch rivalry.
accepted.tq: Identify the outcome of the diplomatic efforts rather than their purpose alone.
accepted.sec: Decline of the Dutch in India - causes

accepted.s:
Which combination contributed to the decline of Dutch power in India?
1. Defeat at Colachel
2. Defeat at Bedara
3. Loss of Andhra strongholds during the Anglo-French wars
4. Priority given to the Indonesian spice monopoly
accepted.x: All four factors contributed to Dutch decline: military defeats, loss of Andhra strongholds and the prioritisation of the Indonesian spice monopoly.
accepted.tq: Combine military, territorial and commercial causes before selecting the comprehensive option.
accepted.sec: Decline of the Dutch in India - causes

accepted.s: The Dutch occupation in India is generally stated to have lasted from:
accepted.x: The period of Dutch occupation in India is stated as 1605–1825.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the broad occupation period from the separate dates of treaty-based cession.
accepted.sec: Decline of the Dutch in India - causes

accepted.s: Which monument is associated with the Dutch presence at Bheemunipatnam?
accepted.x: Bheemunipatnam is associated with a Dutch cemetery, while Fort Geldria is located at Pulicat.
accepted.tq: Match the monument with the correct Andhra location.
accepted.sec: Monuments of Dutch presence in AP

accepted.s: Fort Geldria is located at:
accepted.x: Fort Geldria was established at Pulicat, the major Dutch centre on the Coromandel Coast.
accepted.tq: Use the monument-location association to distinguish Pulicat from other Dutch settlements.
accepted.sec: Monuments of Dutch presence in AP

accepted.s: Which of the following places, along with Palakollu, is identified as an old Dutch settlement in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Palakollu and Draksharama are identified as old Dutch settlements in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Pair the two Andhra settlements rather than confusing them with Dutch centres outside Andhra.
accepted.sec: Monuments of Dutch presence in AP

accepted.s: The Dutch Andhra network extended broadly from:
accepted.x: The Dutch network in Andhra extended from Machilipatnam in the south-western part of the network to Bheemunipatnam in the north-east.
accepted.tq: Test the geographical span of the regional network using its endpoints.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
